B. The thermoacoustic approximation of the piston effect

This section is devoted to analyze the piston effect in supercritical fluids via the developed scheme. In this case the duration of excitation is much longer than the acoustic time scale. Therefore, wave propagation occurs only at the beginning of the process until the initial pressure disturbance reaches the other end of the pipe, correspondingly, no reflection takes place. In order to prove the intensive effect of thermal expansion near the critical point, we present the same phenomenon with same dimensional excitation parameters for an ideal gas state, too. Based on [19], we have defined a cross-section specific heat of q = 30 J mž, to which in the above defined supercritical state the dimensionless value Q = 0.00035 corresponds, the non-dimensional pulse duration fp = 50 and Péclet number Pea = 107 are chosen, which latter implies Rea = 1722695.711.
